mainTopic: Fixing a missing השם in a ספר תורה, and which ruling of רבי שמעון שזורי רבי חנינא was talking about
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about how a סופר fits words at the end of a line. Then a new ברייתא asks what a סופר should do if he left out השם and already wrote the next word. Five תנאים answer, ranging from רבי מאיר, who says the whole sheet must be put away, to רבי יצחק, who allows wiping wet ink and writing השם in its place. רב rules like רבי יוסי that השם may be hung above the line. רבי יצחק בר שמואל rules that one may wipe and write. The גמרא explains that they stated the practice itself because some people mix up who said what. Next, רבי חנינא says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי everywhere, and the גמרא hunts for which of his rulings this was first said about. Each suggestion is rejected because that case already has its own recorded ruling. Finally רב פפא says it was about a chest, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says it was about wine. The explanation of these continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How to split long words and short words at the end of a line
steps.stepSummary: A five-letter word that doesn't fit may be split three letters inside the column and two outside. A two-letter word may not be pushed into the margin; it is written on the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, write three letters inside the column and two outside it. If he reaches a two-letter word, he should not squeeze it into the space between the columns. Instead he writes it at the start of the next line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that began just before this, about a word that doesn't fit at the end of a line. It gives the right way to handle a five-letter word and a two-letter word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a five-letter word, most of the word (three letters) must stay inside the column, and only a smaller part may spill out. A two-letter word is so short that there's no reason to push it out at all, so he simply starts it on the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a column of writing on the parchment
Outside the column, in the margin
A word
A line of writing

phrases.english: Rather, three letters inside the column
and two outside the column.

phrases.aramaic: נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ תֵּיבָה בַּת שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת –
phrases.english: If he comes upon a word of two letters
he should not toss it into the space between the columns,
rather, he goes back and writes it at the start of the next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שָׁלֹשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הַדַּף וּשְׁתַּיִם חוּץ לַדַּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא from the end of the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five-letter word: three inside the column, two outside. Two-letter word: never in the margin; start it on the next line.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: scrape the wrong word off and write God's Name in its place
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if a סופר skipped השם, רבי יהודה says he scrapes off the word he wrote, writes that word above the line, and writes השם in the scraped spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone made a mistake with השם, he scrapes off what he wrote, hangs the scraped word above the line, and writes השם on the scraped spot. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a סופר who forgot to write השם and already wrote the next word. רבי יהודה gives the first way to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה wants השם to sit in its proper place on the line, not squeezed above it. So the other word is the one that gets moved up, and השם takes the main spot.

keyTerms.meaning: One who made a mistake with God's Name, here by leaving it out
Scrapes off dried ink
Hangs, meaning writes small above the line
The spot that was scraped

phrases.english: One who made a mistake with the Name,
phrases.notes: He left out God's Name and already wrote the next word in its place.

phrases.english: scrapes off what he wrote,
and hangs what he scraped off above the line,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוֹתֵב אֶת הַשֵּׁם עַל מְקוֹם הַגְּרָר,
phrases.english: and writes the Name on the scraped spot;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַטּוֹעֶה בַּשֵּׁם, גּוֹרֵר אֶת מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: fixing a missing השם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scrape off the wrong word, write it above the line, and write השם on the scraped spot.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: God's Name itself may be written above the line
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי is more lenient: the סופר may even write השם itself above the line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: One may even hang השם above the line.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא, רבי יוסי, adds a more lenient option to רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה only allowed the ordinary word to be hung. רבי יוסי says the word "even" (אף): השם itself may also be written above the line, so there is no need to scrape anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, adding a further option
Writing God's Name small above the line
Hanging, the general idea of writing a missed word above the line

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
One may even hang the Name above the line.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף תּוֹלִין אֶת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה by allowing a more lenient fix.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: השם itself may be written above the line.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: one may even wipe off wet ink and write the Name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק adds another option: the סופר may wipe off the wrong word and write השם in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: He may even wipe it off and write.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא, רבי יצחק, adds another allowed way to fix the mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה spoke about scraping (גורר). רבי יצחק says one may "even" wipe away the word (מוחק) and write השם in that place.

keyTerms.meaning: Wipes off ink, usually while it is still wet
Wipes off the wrong word and writes the right one there

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
He may even wipe it off and write.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר: אַף מוֹחֵק וְכוֹתֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion, also more lenient than רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may wipe off the wrong word and write השם in its place.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי: hang the whole Name, but never part of it
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי allows hanging השם above the line only if all of it is written there, not just some of its letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: The whole Name may be hung above the line, but part of it may not.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth תנא sets a limit on hanging השם above the line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that השם may go above the line. But the Name may not be split, with some letters on the line and some above it. It must be kept whole in one place.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire Name, all its letters
Part of it
One may not hang it above the line

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
The entire Name may be hung above the line,
part of it may not be hung.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַשֵּׁם כּוּלּוֹ תּוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the idea of hanging השם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole Name may be hung; part of it may not.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: no fix is allowed, so the whole sheet is put away
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says השם may not be written on a scraped or wiped spot, and may not be hung. The whole sheet must be removed and put into גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: One may not write השם on a scraped spot or on a wiped spot, and one may not hang it. So what does he do? He removes the whole sheet and puts it away in גניזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The last and strictest opinion in the ברייתא rejects every fix the others offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר rules out all three methods: scraping, wiping, and hanging. Since none is fitting for השם, the only option is to take out the whole sheet and put it away respectfully.

keyTerms.meaning: The spot that was wiped off
A sheet of parchment in a ספר תורה
Removes
Puts it away respectfully in גניזה instead of throwing it out

steps.whatToRemember: Five views on a missed השם, from strict to lenient: רבי מאיר (put the sheet away), רבי יהודה (scrape and write השם in place), רבי שמעון שזורי (hang only the whole Name), רבי יוסי (hang השם), רבי יצחק (even wipe and write).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
One may not write the Name
neither on a scraped spot
nor on a wiped spot,
and one may not hang it above the line.
So what does he do?
He removes the entire sheet and puts it away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects all the fixes offered by the earlier תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No scraping, wiping, or hanging for השם. The whole sheet is removed and put in גניזה.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree about the practical הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי יוסי that השם may be hung above the line. רבי יצחק בר שמואל rules like רבי יצחק that one may wipe and write.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב חננאל said in the name of רב: The הלכה is that one may hang השם. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יצחק בר שמואל: The הלכה is that one may wipe off and write.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reports how later אמוראים ruled in practice. They disagree with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings pick one of the lenient views from the ברייתא. רב follows רבי יוסי (hang השם). רבי יצחק בר שמואל follows רבי יצחק (wipe and write). Neither rules like the strict view of רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical ruling we follow
A disagreement between sages
A final practical decision

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the אמוראים lean lenient: either hang השם above the line (רב) or wipe off and write it (רבי יצחק בר שמואל).

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Chananel said in the name of Rav:
The halacha is: one may hang the Name above the line.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel:
The halacha is: he wipes off and writes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב, הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the practical הלכה among the views of the ברייתא, though the אמוראים disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: hang השם. רבי יצחק בר שמואל: wipe off and write השם.

steps.title: Why not just name the Sage the הלכה follows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב and רבי יצחק בר שמואל described the actual practice instead of simply saying 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי' and 'the הלכה follows רבי יצחק.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let this Sage say 'the הלכה follows that Sage,' and the other Sage say 'the הלכה follows that Sage.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by how the two rulings in step 7 were worded. It asks why they didn't just name the תנא they agree with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רב said 'one hangs השם' and רבי יצחק בר שמואל said 'one wipes and writes.' The normal, shorter way would be 'הלכה כרבי יוסי' and 'הלכה כרבי יצחק.' So the גמרא wants to know why they chose the longer wording.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him say. This asks why a different wording was not used.
A respectful word for a Sage, like 'the master'
The practical law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: But let this Sage say: the halacha follows that Sage,
phrases.notes: This is רב, who could have just said 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.'

phrases.english: and let this Sage say: the halacha follows that Sage!
phrases.notes: This is רבי יצחק בר שמואל, who could have just said 'the הלכה follows רבי יצחק.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the rulings of step 7 were worded
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אמוראים stated the practice itself rather than naming the תנא they followed

steps.title: Because some people swap the opinions
steps.stepSummary: They described the practice itself because some people reverse which תנא holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there are those who reverse them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Naming the Sage could cause confusion, because some people mix up who said what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone has the names switched, 'הלכה כרבי יוסי' would lead him to the wrong practice. Stating the practice itself ('hang it' or 'wipe and write') leaves no room for that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: They reverse them. Some people swap which opinion belongs to which Sage.

phrases.english: Because there are those who reverse them.
phrases.notes: Meaning, some people switch which opinion belongs to רבי יוסי and which belongs to רבי יצחק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Stating the practice itself avoids mistakes by people who have the opinions reversed
steps.whatToRemember: When opinions might get mixed up, a ruling is safer if it states the practice itself instead of naming a Sage.

steps.title: The הלכה always follows רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules like רבי שמעון שזורי, and adds that the הלכה follows him in every place he taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר חיננא said in the name of עולא, who said in the name of רבי חנינא: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. And more than that: wherever רבי שמעון שזורי taught, the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought in. רבי חנינא says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, and not only in one case but in all his teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts here: a ruling about one specific case, and a general rule for all of רבי שמעון שזורי's teachings. The ruling doesn't say which case the first part is about, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more...
Every place where he taught
The הלכה follows him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר חִינָּנָא, אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Chinnana said that Ulla said that Rabbi Chanina said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,
and not only that, but

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי,
phrases.english: in every place where Rabbi Shimon Shezuri taught,
the halacha follows him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר חִינָּנָא, אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling about one of the opinions listed earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in one specific case and in all his teachings
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a general rule for deciding the הלכה whenever רבי שמעון שזורי disagrees with others.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי שמעון שזורי is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי רבי חנינא was ruling on. It first suggests our case: the whole of השם may be hung above the line, but not part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is it about? If you say it is about this one: 'רבי שמעון שזורי says: the whole השם may be hung, part of it may not be hung'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know which case the first part of רבי חנינא's ruling refers to. It tries out the obvious candidate, our case from step 5, and sets up a challenge to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first guess is רבי שמעון שזורי's rule about hanging השם. The sentence is not finished here. The next step shows why this guess runs into trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? Which case is this about?
If you would say... This puts forward a possibility that will be tested.
We hang it. The word is written above the line.
Part of it

phrases.english: To which one does this refer?
If you say it refers to this one:
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from step 5.

phrases.english: the entire name may be hung above the line,
but part of it may not be hung,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case the ruling of step 10 refers to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי רבי חנינא was ruling on

steps.title: It can't be our case, because the rulings on it never mention him
steps.stepSummary: The rulings already stated about this ברייתא were by רב (hang השם) and by רבי יצחק בר שמואל (wipe and write). If the הלכה followed רבי שמעון שזורי here, that ruling should have been stated alongside them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already stated about it: רב חננאל said in the name of רב, the הלכה is that we hang השם; and רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יצחק בר שמואל, the הלכה is that one wipes and writes. If it is so, let him also state it there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the guess from step 11. The rulings on our ברייתא are well known, and none of them says 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי חנינא's ruling were about hanging השם, it would have been quoted together with the other rulings on this very ברייתא. Since it was left out, it seems רבי חנינא was talking about a different teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי. The גמרא's answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Wipes off the mistaken word and writes השם in its place
And if it were so
Let him also say it. He should have been quoted together with the others.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it,
Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
The halacha is that one hangs the name above the line,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel said:
The halacha is that one wipes and writes.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: If רבי חנינא's ruling really were about this case.

phrases.english: let him also state it there.
phrases.notes: His ruling should have been listed together with these other rulings on the same ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion made in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי חנינא's ruling refers to hanging the whole השם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rulings stated on this ברייתא leave out any ruling like רבי שמעון שזורי. If such a ruling existed for this case, it would have been quoted with them.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting רבי חנינא's ruling. It is only questioning which case that ruling is about.

steps.title: Maybe he meant the calf of a slaughtered cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's view that the slaughter of a mother cow permits the calf found inside her, even years later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant this teaching: רבי שמעון שזורי says that even if the calf is five years old and plowing in the field, the slaughter of its mother makes it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Our case did not work, so the גמרא offers a different teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי that רבי חנינא might have meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a pregnant cow is slaughtered and a live calf is found inside, רבי שמעון שזורי holds that the mother's שחיטה counts for the calf too. He says this holds even if the calf grows up and works in the field. The גמרא tests whether this is the case רבי חנינא ruled on.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it was about this (teaching)
The ritual slaughter of its mother
Makes it permitted (here: permitted to eat without its own שחיטה)
Plowing in the field: a fully grown, working animal

phrases.english: Rather, it was about this:
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even if it is five years old
and plowing in the field,
phrases.notes: This is the calf that was found alive inside a cow when the cow was slaughtered.

phrases.english: the slaughter of its mother makes it permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12 rejected our ברייתא, this offers a new candidate teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the ruling to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא was ruling on the case in our sugya.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי חנינא was ruling on the calf of a slaughtered cow.

steps.title: That ruling was already reported separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the calf case, because זעירי already reported in רבי חנינא's name that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already said about that case: זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. If the general ruling were about that case, it should also have been said there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the calf suggestion. A separate report of רבי חנינא's ruling already exists for that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like step 12. If רבי חנינא's specific ruling 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי' were about the calf case, it would have been reported there, alongside זעירי's report. Since it was not, the calf case cannot be the one meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows (this opinion)
And if it were so
He too should have said it

phrases.english: But it was already said about it:
Ze'eiri said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri.
And if it were so, he too should have said it.
phrases.notes: If רבי חנינא's specific ruling were about this case, it should have been reported there together with זעירי's report.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 13 using the same reasoning as step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי חנינא was ruling on the calf case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling of רבי חנינא on that case is already reported separately by זעירי, so the general ruling would have appeared there.

steps.title: He meant the case of a dangerously ill man ordering a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's view in the case of the גט: even a dangerously ill man who says 'write a גט' is understood to mean 'and give it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant this: At first they said that a man led out in a neck-chain to be executed who says 'write a גט for my wife' means they should write it and give it. Later they added a man setting sail or leaving with a caravan. רבי שמעון שזורי says: even a dangerously ill man.
steps.whatsHappening: The calf case did not work, so the גמרא tries another teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי that רבי חנינא might have meant. Step 17 will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband must order that the גט be given, not just written. In urgent cases where he is about to die or vanish, the חכמים assume he wants it given too. רבי שמעון שזורי extends this to a dangerously ill man, and the גמרא tests whether this is the case רבי חנינא meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A neck-chain put on someone led to execution
Bill of divorce
They should write it and give it
One who sets sail on a sea voyage
Caravan traveling far away
One who is dangerously ill

phrases.english: Rather, it was about this:
At first they would say:
One who is led out in a neck-chain
phrases.notes: He is being taken out to be executed.

phrases.english: and said, 'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,'
these people should write it and give it.
They later said:
Even one who sets sail, and one who leaves with a caravan.
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even one who is dangerously ill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the calf case was rejected in step 14, a new teaching is offered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the ruling to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא was ruling on the calf case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי חנינא was ruling on the dangerously ill man who orders a גט (rejected in step 17).

steps.title: Or he meant the case of mixed תרומת מעשר of דמאי
steps.stepSummary: Another option: רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's view that when תרומת מעשר of דמאי gets mixed back in, one may ask the seller and rely on him even on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else he meant this: תרומת מעשר of דמאי that went back into its original produce. רבי שמעון שזורי says: even on a weekday one may ask him and eat based on what he says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second possible teaching that רבי חנינא might have meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is produce bought from someone who may not have tithed properly. On שבת, when one cannot separate tithes, the חכמים allowed asking the seller and relying on his answer. רבי שמעון שזורי allows this on a weekday too when the separated תרומת מעשר got mixed back in, and רבי חנינא may have been ruling on this.

keyTerms.meaning: Or else; another possibility
The portion of the tithe that the לוי gives to a כהן
Produce of an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed
That went back into the produce it was taken from
Asks him and eats based on his word

phrases.english: Or else, it was about this:
Teruma of the tithe of demai
that went back to its place,
phrases.notes: It got mixed back into the same produce it was separated from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even on a weekday
one may ask him and eat based on his word.
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the עם הארץ who sold the produce. You ask whether he tithed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second possible case alongside step 15; both are rejected in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling must be about the גט case only.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may instead be about mixed תרומת מעשר of דמאי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן already ruled on the sick man and the דמאי cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects both earlier suggestions. רבי יוחנן already said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case of the dangerously ill man and the case of תרומת מעשר of דמאי. If רבי חנינא had ruled on these too, his ruling would have been reported together with רבי יוחנן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about these: רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case of the dangerously ill man and in the case of תרומת מעשר of דמאי? If רבי חנינא was talking about these, his ruling should have been said there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the two answers from steps 15 and 16. Those cases already have a recorded ruling, from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same logic as step 12. If a ruling on a case was already reported, רבי חנינא's matching ruling should have been mentioned with it. Since it was not, his statement must be about some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: A dangerously ill person; here, the man who said 'write a גט'
The portion the לוי gives to a כהן out of the מעשר he received
Produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it properly
The practical law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: But wasn't it already stated about it
Rabbi Yochanan said
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri
in the case of the dangerously ill man, and in the case of teruma of the tithe of demai
phrases.notes: These are exactly the two cases suggested in steps 15 and 16.

phrases.english: And if it is so
let him also say it
phrases.notes: He means: רבי חנינא's ruling should have been reported right there next to רבי יוחנן's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answers given in steps 15 and 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי חנינא ruled on the גט case or the דמאי case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases already have a recorded ruling from רבי יוחנן. If רבי חנינא had ruled on them, his ruling would have been recorded alongside it.

steps.title: New suggestion: the bean that took root on both sides of the New Year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רבי חנינא ruled on רבי שמעון שזורי's law about the Egyptian bean. If some plants took root before ראש השנה and some after, one may not separate from one group for the other. The solution is to pile it all together, so that he separates new for new and old for old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was about this: רבי יוסי בן כיפר says in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי: if someone planted an Egyptian bean for its seed, and some took root before ראש השנה and some after, he may not take תרומה from one group for the other. That is because one may not take תרומה and מעשר from the new year's crop for the old, or from the old for the new. What should he do? He piles all his crop into the middle of his threshing floor. Then it turns out he separates from the new in it for the new in it, and from the old in it for the old in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new candidate for רבי חנינא's ruling. It is רבי שמעון שזורי's solution for beans that took root partly in the old year and partly in the new year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crops of different years cannot cover each other for תרומה and מעשר, and you cannot tell which plants rooted when. רבי שמעון שזורי's idea is to mix everything thoroughly. Then whatever he separates contains new and old in the same proportion as the whole pile, so each year's crop is covered by its own produce.

keyTerms.meaning: The Egyptian bean (cowpea), a plant that can be grown for its seeds
Took root; for this plant, the year is fixed by when it rooted
The new year's crop and the old year's crop
He piles his crop into the middle of his threshing floor, mixing it all together

phrases.english: Rather, it was about this
Rabbi Yosei ben Kifar says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri
An Egyptian bean that someone planted for its seed
some of it took root before Rosh HaShana
and some of it after Rosh HaShana
one may not separate teruma from this for that
because one may not separate teruma and tithes
from the new crop for the old
nor from the old crop for the new
How should he act?
He piles his crop into the middle of his threshing floor
and it turns out that he separates teruma and tithes

phrases.aramaic: מִן הֶחָדָשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הֶחָדָשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ
phrases.english: from the new crop in it for the new crop in it

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ
phrases.english: and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 rejects the גט and דמאי cases, this offers a new case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the ruling to a different case of רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's ruling was about the גט or דמאי case
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי חנינא's ruling was about the Egyptian bean case

steps.title: רבי יוחנן already ruled on the bean case too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the bean suggestion. רבי שמואל בר נחמני already reported in רבי יוחנן's name that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in this case. If רבי חנינא had ruled on it too, that should have been mentioned there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about this: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי? If רבי חנינא was talking about this, his ruling should have been said there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the bean suggestion from step 18 with the same argument it has been using. This case also already has a recorded ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats from steps 12, 14 and 17. Any case that already has a recorded ruling cannot be where רבי חנינא's statement belongs, or his ruling would have been reported with it. So the search for the right case continues.

keyTerms.meaning: About it; referring back to the ברייתא just quoted
And if it were so; introduces what should have happened if the suggestion were true
Let him also say it; his ruling should have appeared there too

steps.whatToRemember: Every case of רבי שמעון שזורי suggested so far (the calf, the גט, דמאי, the bean) already has a recorded ruling. That is why the גמרא keeps rejecting each one as the case רבי חנינא was talking about.

phrases.english: Wasn't it already stated about it
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yochanan said
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri
And if it is so
let him also say it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the bean suggestion of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי חנינא ruled on the Egyptian bean case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's ruling on this case was already reported through רבי שמואל בר נחמני. If רבי חנינא had ruled on it, his ruling should have been recorded with it.

steps.title: רב פפא: It was the case of the chest
steps.stepSummary: After the earlier suggestions were rejected, רב פפא offers a new answer: רבי חנינא's ruling was about רבי שמעון שזורי's law about a chest (שידה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: It was about the chest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the earlier ideas and offers a fresh answer. רב פפא says רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's view about a chest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every earlier case already had its own recorded ruling (from רב and רבי יצחק בר שמואל, from זעירי, or from רבי יוחנן), so none could be what רבי חנינא meant. רב פפא picks a different ruling of רבי שמעון שזורי that has no other recorded ruling, so this problem does not come up. The details of the chest case come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier ideas are dropped and a new answer is coming.
A large chest or box

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא is arguing about the הלכה itself. Everyone agrees the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. The question is only which of his rulings רבי חנינא was talking about.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
It was about the chest.
phrases.notes: He means רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's law about a chest. The גמרא explains it soon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bean suggestion was rejected in Step 19, this offers a new case that has no other recorded ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks a new subject for רבי חנינא's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's ruling was about the גט, the תרומת מעשר of דמאי, or the Egyptian bean.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב פפא, רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's law about a chest.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: It was the case of the wine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a different answer: רבי חנינא's ruling was about רבי שמעון שזורי's law about wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It was about the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to the same question. רב נחמן בר יצחק says רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's view about wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second option, side by side with רב פפא's. It also picks a ruling of רבי שמעון שזורי that רבי יוחנן did not mention. The details of the wine case are explained later.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It was about the wine.
phrases.notes: Another case of רבי שמעון שזורי. The גמרא gives the details later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing answer to the same question that רב פפא answered in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks a different new subject for רבי חנינא's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's ruling was about one of the cases that already had a recorded ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, רבי חנינא was ruling on רבי שמעון שזורי's law about wine.

steps.title: Starting to explain רב פפא's answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain in detail what רב פפא meant by "the chest."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to explain רב פפא's answer, the chest case, in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only heard one word from each אמורא: "chest" and "wine." Now the גמרא goes back to fill in what רב פפא meant. The explanation continues in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to Step 20 to start explaining רב פפא's short answer in detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רב פפא's detailed explanation of the chest case. The content continues beyond this line.
